sections.title: Foundations & Architecture
sections.description: The zero-build runtime model, global script contract, and source-of-truth philosophy.

entries.title: Zero-build vanilla JS & UMD architecture
entries.summary: Pure domain modules in src/*.js pair with classic browser scripts in src/app/*.js without a bundler.
entries.what: Runs directly in any modern browser (`app.html`) or inside the Tauri v2 desktop shell with zero frontend build tools and zero npm runtime dependencies.
how: 12 pure UMD modules in `src/*.js` expose stateless parsers, bundlers, and storage helpers that run identically in the browser and in Node.js unit tests (`test/run.js`).
19 classic `<script>` files in `src/app/*.js` share a single global scope in `app.html` (`core.js` first, `main.js` last).
`test/structure.test.js` verifies script load order, no duplicate top-level declarations, a 500-line ceiling per `src/app/*.js` file, and Service Worker `APP_FILES` parity.
entries.why: Recorded in D-001: avoiding Vite/Webpack/React eliminates build-step fragility, keeps the entire studio inspectable as plain files, and allows instant unit testing in Node.js without DOM shims.

entries.title: Non-destructive HTML5 and CSS byte-offset splicing
entries.summary: Visual edits splice exact character spans in user source files instead of serializing live DOM innerHTML.
entries.what: Parses HTML5 (`HtmlAst`) and CSS (`CssAst`) into offset-indexed syntax trees and performs surgical edits (`setAttr`, `setText`, `insertElement`, `moveElement`, `duplicateElement`, `setProperty`) while keeping user formatting, indentation, and comments intact.
how: `HtmlAst.parse()` records exact `start`, `end`, `openStart`, `openEnd`, `closeStart`, and `attrSpans` character offsets plus line numbers for every element.
`HtmlAst.stamp()` injects ephemeral `data-pc-id` and `data-line` attributes only into the preview HTML sent to `#stageFrame`, never into `projectFiles.entries`.
`CssAst.parse()` indexes rules and declarations with exact byte ranges so Inspector edits and `findRuleBySelector()` modify only the targeted declaration.
entries.why: Recorded in D-003: serializing `stageFrame.contentDocument.documentElement.outerHTML` would destroy author whitespace, reorder attributes, and leak runtime bridge markers into user files.

entries.title: Transparent-textarea syntax shader & block highlighter
entries.summary: A synchronized background layer paints HTML/CSS/JS token colors and Stage selection highlights behind #editor.
entries.what: Provides live syntax coloring for HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, Emmet-lite tag abbreviation expansion on `Tab`, smart `Enter` auto-indentation, and line-range highlighting (`highlightCodeRange`) when an element is clicked on the Stage.
how: `#editor` is a transparent-text `<textarea>` positioned over `.editor-shade` (`src/app/shade.js`).
`CodeShade.shade()` (`src/code-shade.js`) tokenizes each line and wraps Stage-selected line ranges in `.sh-selected-line`.
`checkShade()` verifies line-wrap alignment between the textarea and the background layer, falling back to plain text if browser zoom or font metrics ever diverge.
entries.why: Recorded in D-002: delivers responsive code editing and visual block highlighting in a few hundred lines of vanilla JS without bundling megabytes of Monaco or CodeMirror.

sections.title: The WYSIWYG Design Stage & Inspector
sections.description: Direct manipulation on the Stage iframe, live text editing, and the dockable/floating CSS Designer.

entries.title: Focus-preserving Stage selection & single-click text editing
entries.summary: Clicking an element on the Design Stage highlights its code block while keeping keyboard focus in the Stage for direct text editing.
entries.what: Allows users to click any text element (`h1`-`h6`, `p`, `span`, `a`, `button`, `li`, `td`, etc.) on the Design Stage and immediately type or edit text in place while watching the corresponding HTML code block highlight and update live in the Code pane.
how: Clicking on the Stage sends `{ type: 'pc-select', id }` to the parent window, which calls `selectElementById(id, { scrollEditor: true, focusEditor: false })` so `#editor` scrolls and highlights `.sh-selected-line` without stealing keyboard focus.
In `src/app/stage.js`, clicking a text-editable element immediately activates `contenteditable="true"` and positions the caret at the pointer coordinates via `caretRangeFromPoint`.
Keystrokes inside the Stage emit `pc-inline-input`, which splices the updated text via `HtmlAst.setText()` with `skipStageRender: true` so the iframe DOM is not blown away mid-typing.
entries.why: Recorded in D-009: focusing `#editor` on Stage click caused subsequent keystrokes to overwrite the selected HTML block in Code mode rather than editing the text naturally on the Design Stage.

entries.title: Pointer-based Stage drag-and-drop & badge quick actions
entries.summary: Deterministic pointer tracking reorders elements before, after, or inside targets with live amber drop guides.
entries.what: Reorders elements on the Design Stage by dragging any element (or dragging the `⠿` handle on the floating stage badge while text editing), and provides one-click badge buttons for Move Up (`↑`), Move Down (`↓`), Duplicate (`⧉`), and Delete (`✕`).
how: Tracks `mousedown`, `mousemove`, and `mouseup` inside the Stage bridge (`src/app/stage.js`) with a 5px movement threshold.

Computes whether the pointer is in the top 28% (`before`), bottom 28% (`after`), or middle (`inside` for containers, otherwise nearest edge) of the hovered target, drawing `[data-pc-drop-target]` guide lines.
On `mouseup`, posts `pc-move-to` to the parent window, which executes a single-pass byte-offset splice in `HtmlAst.moveElement()`.
entries.why: Recorded in D-008: native HTML5 `draggable="true"` / `dragover` / `drop` events inside an `iframe[srcdoc]` abort drops on Linux WebKitGTK when releasing over margins or dragging links/buttons, and two-pass insert+remove shifts `data-pc-id` numbering.

entries.title: Dockable / floating Inspector & Rich CSS Designer
entries.summary: Inspects HTML attributes, live getComputedStyle values, visual box-model overlays, and jumps to CSS rules.
entries.what: Provides an HTML Properties editor and a 5-section Rich CSS Designer (Layout, Spacing & Box Model, Size, Typography, Background & Border) that can be docked at the bottom, top, left, or right of the Stage from its **Dock** menu (side docks are a resizable single column), collapsed to its header bar, popped out as a draggable floating window, or hidden (`Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+I`).
how: When an element is selected on the Stage, the bridge reads `window.getComputedStyle(el)` and `getBoundingClientRect()` and posts them to `src/app/inspector-ui.js`.
Inputs display live computed values as placeholders while editing either inline `style` (`HtmlAst.setAttr`) or linked stylesheet rules (`CssAst.setProperty`).

Hovering or editing Box Model inputs draws amber margin and emerald padding overlays on the Stage; clicking **Go to CSS ↗** locates the rule via `CssAst.findRuleBySelector()` and highlights it in the Code editor.
entries.why: Recorded in D-007 and D-016: real-world stylesheets often define rules across multiple selectors or external defaults; surfacing `getComputedStyle` alongside declared CSS rules and allowing floating/collapsible panel states keeps the Stage spacious and informative.

entries.title: In-app JS Console
entries.summary: Shows Live JS console output, errors, and rejections in an Inspector tab with click-to-jump source lines.
entries.what: A third Inspector tab (`Console`) lists `console.log/info/warn/error` calls, uncaught errors, and unhandled promise rejections from the Live JS Stage, filterable by All / Errors / Warnings / Logs, with an unread badge and a Clear button. Errors carry a `file:line` link that opens the file and selects the line in the Code editor.
how: In Live JS mode `Project.assemblePreview` injects `Project.consoleBridge` before user scripts; it wraps the console methods, `window.onerror`, and `unhandledrejection` and posts `pc-console` messages to the parent window.
`assemblePreview` records the document line where each user script starts and passes the map to the bridge, which converts `window.onerror` line numbers to project-file lines.
`src/app/console-ui.js` stores up to 500 entries, renders rows, and clears them whenever the Stage re-renders because scripts re-run.
entries.why: Recorded in D-011: devtools-free runtime feedback needs a channel from Live JS to the Studio, and removing the old `try/catch` wrapper gives exact error lines and real-page `let`/`const` scoping.

entries.title: Multi-page link navigation on the Stage
entries.summary: Following a relative link on the Stage opens the linked project page in the Studio.
entries.what: In Live JS mode a normal click on a relative link opens the linked `.html` file in the Studio. In Design mode `Ctrl/Cmd+Click`, the `Follow ↗` badge button, or **Follow Link ↗** in Properties does the same, while a plain click still selects and edits the link text.
how: The Live bridge in `src/app/stage-live.js` cancels clicks on relative, non-anchor links that page scripts did not handle and posts `pc-navigate`; Design-mode actions post `pc-navigate` or `pc-follow-link`.

`Project.resolveRelativePath(fromFile, rawHref)` normalizes `./`, `../`, `?query`, `#hash`, and encoded paths, and returns nothing for `http:`, `mailto:`, `tel:`, `javascript:`, `data:`, `//`, or same-page anchors.
`followProjectLink()` opens the target with `openFileInEditor()` only when it is an `.html` file in the project; otherwise it shows a notice.
entries.why: Recorded in D-012: the iframe cannot see project files, so it only cancels navigation and the Studio decides, which keeps the Stage from navigating away from the active document and keeps D-009 text editing intact.

entries.title: Binary project assets in the browser build
entries.summary: Images, fonts, and other binaries from an opened folder render on the Stage and survive reload.
entries.what: When a folder is opened in a Chromium browser, non-text files (up to 25 MB each, 200 MB per project) are kept with the project so relative `src`, `srcset`, `poster`, `<link href>`, and CSS `url()` references display on the Stage. The desktop app does not need this because it serves files over localhost.
how: `scanBrowserDir()` in `src/app/tauri-files.js` collects binaries as Blobs; `src/app/assets.js` creates `blob:` URLs and saves the Blobs to the IndexedDB `assets` store keyed by project.
`Project.assemblePreview()` rewrites matching relative references through `Project.rewriteAssetUrls()` and `rewriteCssUrls()`; stylesheet URLs resolve relative to the stylesheet file.
Assets are loaded again when the project opens, copied on Duplicate, removed when the trash purge deletes the project, and written by **Export to a new folder**.
entries.why: Recorded in D-013: the `srcdoc` Stage resolves relative URLs against the app origin, and persisting Blobs separately keeps the single-string pack format of D-004 and the isolated workspace of D-006.

entries.title: Shared page parts (marker regions)
entries.summary: Reuse a header or footer across pages while every page stays plain HTML.
entries.what: **Make Part…** moves the selected element into a project file such as `parts/header.html` and leaves a `<!-- pc:part src="..." -->` region in the page. Pages can include the same part, editing the part file updates all of them, and the **Parts** Inspector tab lists parts, flags pages whose copy differs, and inserts a part into the current page.
how: `src/parts.js` finds marker regions in every `.html` entry, resolves `src` with `Project.resolveRelativePath`, and reports each region as synced, differs, or missing; unmatched or nested markers are reported and never rewritten.

`propagatePartEdits()` runs inside `render()`: when the active file is a part, `Parts.sync()` rewrites only the text between markers in every page that references it, in the same undo step as the edit.
A page that differs from its part offers **Use part** (overwrite the region) or **Update part** (`Parts.pull()` makes the part match, then syncs every other page).
entries.why: Recorded in D-014: duplicating the part inside each page keeps every file valid standalone HTML (D-003) with no include directive or build step, at the cost of duplicated markup and syncing that overwrites local edits made inside a region.

entries.title: Line-number gutter and Find / Replace
entries.summary: Line numbers that follow wrapped lines, plus in-file and project-wide find and replace with undo.
entries.what: The code editor shows line numbers (highlighting the caret line and the Stage-selected block). `Ctrl/Cmd+F` opens a find bar that highlights every match in the current file; `Ctrl/Cmd+H` focuses the Replace box. `Enter` and `Shift+Enter` step through matches, `Aa` toggles case matching, and **Replace** / **Replace All** edit the file. The **Project** toggle (`Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F`) lists matches in every file, lets you exclude files, and replaces across the project in one undo step.
how: `drawGutter()` in `src/app/shade.js` lays the lines out in a hidden copy of the editor to learn each wrapped line's height, so row `n` lines up with line `n`.
`Finding.findAll()` (`src/finding.js`) returns literal, non-overlapping match offsets; `src/app/find.js` draws them as `<mark>` elements on a transparent layer under the text.

Replacements go through `applyEdit()` with a minimal `Editing.diffEdit()` change, so they are one undo step in the project-wide history; project scope uses `Finding.findInFiles()` / `replaceInFiles()` and commits every changed file together (D-019).
entries.why: Recorded in D-015: measuring from a hidden mirror and drawing matches on their own layer keeps both features working when syntax colours are off, which is the failure mode of the transparent-textarea editor of D-002.

entries.title: Top menu bar, Insert dropdown, and right-click context menu
entries.summary: Unified element insertion and DOM manipulation from the top menu bar or right-click context menu.
entries.what: Places the primary Studio command bar (`Projects`, `Open Folder`, `Insert ▾`, `Undo`, `Redo`, `History`, `Export`, `Inspector`, `Settings`, `Help`) above the file tab strip and provides an **Insert Element** submenu inside the right-click context menu on both the Design Stage and HTML editor.
how: `#insertMenuBtn` opens `#insertDropdown` to insert semantic HTML5 snippets (`header`, `nav`, `section`, `div`, `p`, `h1`, `h2`, `button`, `a`, `img`, `ul`, `form`, `input`, `table`) inside the selected Stage element or at the Code caret.

Right-clicking any element on the Stage (`pc-contextmenu`) or inside `#editor` opens `#contextMenu` (`src/app/inspector-ui.js`) with Select Parent, Move Up/Down, Duplicate, Edit/Jump to CSS, Delete, and the **Insert Element ▸** flyout.
entries.why: Keeps the workspace uncluttered by replacing the permanent secondary element chip bar with a compact dropdown and context-sensitive right-click menu.

sections.title: Multi-File Workspace, Undo/Redo & Tauri Desktop I/O
sections.description: How multi-file projects, undo history, local folders, and static assets are managed safely.

entries.title: Problems tab (broken-link checker)
entries.summary: Finds broken links and missing files across the whole project and jumps to each one.
entries.what: The **Problems** Inspector tab lists dead page links, missing images, media, stylesheets, and scripts, CSS `url()` and `@import` targets, links that leave the project, case-only matches, extensionless links, and `#anchor` targets with no matching element. A badge shows the count (red when any is an error), and clicking a row opens the file and selects the exact attribute or URL.
how: `Links.createChecker()` in `src/links.js` extracts references from every `.html` file through `HtmlAst` (so commented-out markup is ignored) and every `.css` file, caching the result per file text.

Each reference is resolved with `Project.resolveRelativePath` against the project's files plus binary files from the folder tree; a missing target is an error, while case-only matches, extensionless links, and missing fragments are warnings.
`src/app/problems-ui.js` re-checks 500 ms after edits and whenever the tab opens, and jumps with `openFileInEditor()` plus a selection of the reported range.
entries.why: Recorded in D-018: renames, deletions, and hand edits break links in pages other than the one being edited, and static checking catches them without running anything, at the cost of not seeing URLs built in JavaScript.

entries.title: Explorer file operations and unsaved dots
entries.summary: Rename, duplicate, and delete project files with link updates, undo, and per-file unsaved markers.
entries.what: Hovering or right-clicking a file in the Explorer offers **Rename**, **Duplicate**, and **Delete**. Renaming or moving a file rewrites links to it (`href`, `src`, `poster`, CSS `url()`, and shared-part markers); the last `.html` file cannot be deleted. Tabs and Explorer rows show a `•` when a file differs from the last load, explicit **Save**, or **Export**.
how: `Project.renameFile()`, `duplicateFile()`, `deleteFile()`, and `treeAfter()` are pure helpers; `src/app/explorer-ui.js` applies them as one project-wide undo step that now also restores the tab list and file tree.
`FileSync.dirtyPaths()` compares the current files with `savedFileEntries`, which is reset on project load, explicit Save (not the 1.5 second auto-save), and Export.
Names are normalized and rejected if they escape the project, contain forbidden characters, or clash with another file ignoring case.
entries.why: Recorded in D-017: renames that left links stale would silently break pages, and clearing the dot on every auto-save would make it meaningless, so the dot tracks explicit saves and exports.

entries.title: Project-wide multi-file Undo and Redo stack
entries.summary: Snapshots all project files, active tabs, and Stage selection across Code, Stage, and Inspector edits.
entries.what: Supports `Ctrl/Cmd+Z` (Undo) and `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z` / `Ctrl+Y` (Redo) plus top-bar `#undoBtn` / `#redoBtn` across all files in the project.
how: `src/app/typing.js` maintains `undoStack` and `redoStack` (up to 150 snapshots), storing a deep clone of `projectFiles.entries`, `activeFile`, `activeHtmlFile`, `selectedPcId`, and editor selection offsets.
Rapid typing in `#editor` coalesces into 600ms bursts (`TYPING_COALESCE_MS`), while every Stage drag/move, inline text edit burst, and Inspector change records a discrete undo checkpoint.
entries.why: Recorded in D-010: native browser `<textarea>` undo is wiped whenever `editor.value` is replaced on a file-tab switch and cannot undo cross-file edits made from the Stage or CSS Designer.

entries.title: Isolated Studio project environment & localhost asset server
entries.summary: Opening a local folder creates a safe Studio workspace with live binary asset rendering and explicit structure-preserving Export.
entries.what: Loads an existing local website folder (including nested subdirectories, multiple `.html`/`.css`/`.js` files, and binary images/fonts) into an isolated Studio project environment without touching local disk until the user explicitly clicks **Export**.
how: In Tauri (`src-tauri/src/main.rs`), `open_project_folder` recursively reads text files into `projectFiles.entries`, records the directory tree, and starts a loopback HTTP static asset server (`127.0.0.1:<port>`) rejecting any `..` path traversal.
`Project.assemblePreview()` injects `<base href="http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<dir>/">` so relative images (`images/photo.jpg`), fonts, and stylesheets render faithfully in `#stageFrame`.

In `src/app/tauri-files.js`, opening a folder creates a new Studio library record (`currentScriptId = newId()`). Auto-save writes only to IndexedDB; clicking **Export → Save Project to Local Folder** writes all files back to disk while retaining the folder and file structure.
entries.why: Recorded in D-006: auto-overwriting a user's existing project folder on every 1.5s studio auto-save risks unintended destructive changes before the user is ready to commit their work to disk.

entries.title: Multi-file IndexedDB persistence & snapshot history
entries.summary: Packs all project files into sentinel-delimited bundles stored in IndexedDB with emergency localStorage fallback.
entries.what: Automatically saves every project edit to IndexedDB (`plainchant_web_db`), supports multiple projects with 30-day soft-delete trash recovery in `#library-modal`, and captures point-in-time project snapshots in `#versions-modal`.
how: `Project.pack()` and `Project.unpack()` (`src/project.js`) serialize `projectFiles.entries` and directory metadata into a single string using `/* === PLAINCHANT:FILE:<path> === */` sentinel markers.
`Store` (`src/store.js`) and `src/app/persistence.js` write the packed record to IndexedDB and mirror unsaved changes to `localStorage['plainchant_web_emergency']` on `beforeunload`.
entries.why: Recorded in D-004: sentinel packing lets `Store`, `Library`, and `Versions` snapshot, diff, and restore entire multi-file websites as atomic records.
